Area.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/8] The selfloathing resulting from sex-stress compromises mental well-being from a very young age (D'Augelli et al. 1998; Johnson et al. 2007; Shildo 1994).[/page/5/Text/10] The unacceptability of being gay often equates to social exclusion (Flowers & Buston 2001; Johnson et al. 2007; Meyer 1995), leading to 'outsiderness' (Smith 1992).[/page/5/Text/11] The detrimental effects of internalized homophobia on one's mental health are well documented (D'Augelli et al. 1998; Flowers & Buston 2001; Robertson 1998).[/page/6/Text/3] For the participants in this study, their coming out to others was not an indicator of self-acceptance, but one of unacceptability that reinforced the self-loathing and desire of wanting to stop the inner conflict. The consequence of this has been the need to destroy the bad part of the self, which they have tried to achieve through their suicidality, the ultimate 'punishment' for their 'crime' of being gay.
